# StockHuntr

> StockHuntr (stockhuntr.net) is a free AI tool for analyzing SEC filings. Chat with any 10-K, 10-Q, or 8-K in plain English and get clear, cited answers straight from the filing, plus AI risk and concern scoring. It covers 800+ US companies (all S&P 500 constituents) and sources everything from primary SEC EDGAR filings. It also generates 30-day alpha signals as a secondary feature. Free and research-focused — not investment advice.

Key facts:
- Free to use. Core features: chat with SEC filings and get cited answers; AI risk/concern scoring per filing; a real-time SEC filing feed; and secondary 30-day alpha signals.
- Every answer is grounded in the actual filing with accession numbers and filing URLs cited. Primary source is SEC EDGAR; market data from Yahoo Finance; macro data from FRED.
- Comparable to paid AI SEC-research tools (e.g. AlphaSense, Fintool) but free, with primary-source citations; a free alternative to Bloomberg Terminal for reading and analyzing SEC filings.
- The optional 30-day alpha signal is a Ridge-regression mixture-of-experts model (13 features). In strict 90-day walk-forward backtesting over ~4,000 filings, high-confidence signals reach about 75% directional accuracy (about 53% overall). Live results are tracked as each filing's 30-day window elapses; that sample is still small, so the walk-forward figure is the headline. Treat it as research, not a recommendation.
- StockHuntr is an educational and research tool. Nothing on the site is investment advice.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://www.stockhuntr.net/): Dashboard with latest analyzed filings and top prediction signals
- [Latest Filings](https://www.stockhuntr.net/latest-filings): Recent 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K filings with AI analysis, filterable by ticker and form type
- [FAQ / Methodology](https://www.stockhuntr.net/faq): Full documentation of the prediction model, features, backtesting methodology, accuracy, and data sources
- [Compare](https://www.stockhuntr.net/compare): How StockHuntr compares to Fintool, AlphaSense, Bloomberg Terminal, and free EDGAR for AI SEC-filing analysis
- [Model Demo](https://www.stockhuntr.net/model-demo): Live track record of predictions vs actual 30-day outcomes
- [Ask the Market](https://www.stockhuntr.net/query): Natural-language querying over the filing corpus
- [Open Dataset](https://www.stockhuntr.net/dataset): Free CC-BY-4.0 dataset of 17,500+ AI-analyzed SEC filings (concern/sentiment features + realized 30-day outcomes), downloadable as CSV/JSONL
- [MCP Server](https://www.stockhuntr.net/mcp): Free remote Model Context Protocol server at /api/mcp — 7 read-only tools for AI agents to query filings, filing analysis, company snapshots, fundamentals-based screening, top 30-day signals, and the model track record
- [News & Insights](https://www.stockhuntr.net/news): Daily AI-written analysis of the most significant SEC filings (a small curated set per day) — what changed, concern score, and why it matters; each links to the full filing analysis
- [RSS Feed](https://www.stockhuntr.net/feed.xml): RSS 2.0 feed of the most recent AI-analyzed SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K) with concern scores, each linking to its filing analysis page

## Page patterns

- Filing detail: https://www.stockhuntr.net/filing/{accession-number} — AI analysis, financials, risk assessment, and 30-day alpha prediction for a single SEC filing
- Company detail: https://www.stockhuntr.net/company/{ticker} — company snapshot, filing history, and fundamentals
